visuals.title: Quiz
visuals.text: Five questions. Answer along on the cards below the transcript, then hear Marco's answers.

quiz.pause_at: Pause here if you want to think it through

questions.q: A company has 800 of assets and 500 of liabilities. What is its equity?
questions.explain: Equity is what's left for the owners: assets minus liabilities, 800 − 500 = 300.
questions.explain_at: One equation. Assets equal liabilities plus equity

questions.q: It issues 50 of new shares for cash. What changes on the balance sheet?
questions.explain: New shareholders hand over cash, so cash and equity both rise by 50. Issuing shares isn't income.
questions.explain_at: or the owners provided it or left profits in the business

questions.q: It then uses 40 of cash to repay debt. What changes?
questions.explain: Both sides fall by 40. Equity doesn't move, because repaying debt isn't an expense.
questions.explain_at: Correct, and that's the full answer. Assets up one hundred

questions.q: A bank has 1,000 of assets and 50 of equity. What's its leverage, and what fall in asset values wipes out the equity?
questions.explain: 1,000 ÷ 50 = 20x. Liabilities don't shrink when assets fall, so a 5% fall eats the whole 50 of equity.
questions.explain_at: That's twenty times. Now, if the value of its assets falls by five percent

questions.q: A company has large retained earnings. Does it have lots of cash?

options.text: Yes, retained earnings sit in the bank
Yes, as long as no dividends were paid
No, retained earnings are a liability
Not necessarily; the profit may be spent

questions.explain: Retained earnings are profit kept in the business, but it may already have gone on machines, new cafés or repaying debt. Check the cash line itself.
questions.explain_at: Same trap, second version. Retained earnings is the running total
